subject: research/selfrep-learnfirst
professional: a design-for-manufacture / open-source-hardware researcher who has studied RepRap self-replication (bill-of-materials closure, Moses and Chirikjian-style analyses) and a statistician reviewing the rank-stability method

evidence.correctness: Ran python3 experiments/run.py: output byte-identical to the committed results.txt (git status clean). Recomputed independently from selfrep_closure.bom.PARTS (own script, not learn.py): 51 lines, 29 with no maker, 468 units, 6359.9 g, 192.34 cost; NEMA17 qty 5 x 280 g /6359.9 = 22.01 points mass, 5x10/192.34 = 25.996 points cost; M8 nut 100/468 = 21.37 units; controller 30/192.34 = 15.60 cost; all match README and results.txt. Also recomputed kind totals (22 makeable lines of 51 = 43.1% lines) and the 3-line cumulative +52.0 cost match. Stability numbers (90%/76%) were only reproduced by rerunning the same seeded code, not independently. Inputs (masses, costs) are the assumed placeholders of selfrep-closure, and the output is only as right as those; the method is arithmetic and is sound.
evidence.completeness: README claims checked: 7 unit tests (7 run, pass); run.py writes results.txt (works); figure.py writes learn_curve.svg (file present, parsed from results.txt); per-metric top lines, lines-to-+10/25/50, Kendall tau table, 2000-draw stability, by-kind table all present in results.txt and match README bullets. Live page link not loaded (offline audit). Next-steps (difficulty model) are honestly listed as not done. No stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests: 7 tests OK. Seeded 4 mutations in learn.py: (1) drop qty from mass gain: caught (1 failure, 1 error); (2) Kendall denominator c+d+1: caught; (3) ranking sort ascending: caught; (4) lines_to_reach threshold changed from run >= target to run > target + 0.2: NOT caught, all 7 pass. Tests also never assert any headline number (NEMA17 first, +22.0, 90%), only identities such as gains summing to 1 and monotonicity, so a changed BOM or tie-break would not fail; no test of by_kind beyond a sum, none of the stability result. Reverted all mutations with git checkout.
evidence.craft: Read learn.py (96 lines), run.py, figure.py, tests, pyproject.toml. Small, clear, deterministic (seeded random.Random), docstrings state the model. Defects: sys.path.insert reaching into sibling selfrep-closure source by relative path, a fragile coupling and the package is not installable standalone despite pyproject saying dependencies = []; top_stability recomputes full gains() for every draw (fine at this size); kendall_tau docstring says no ties but the ranking tie-break is alphabetical, and ties in the lines metric are therefore arbitrary and feed the tau lines-vs-X values (+0.38, +0.26, +0.01), which are mostly an artefact of alphabetical order; run.py writes results.txt on import with no main guard (cosmetic).
evidence.claims: Each headline number traced to results.txt and independently recomputed (see correctness). README states limits clearly: stylised, assumed masses, learning free and certain so upper bound only, fastener lines are wiki box sizes inflating units, line-metric ties are alphabetical not findings, perturbation not a measured spread, nothing built. Weakness: the headline 'the ranking is fairly robust' is stated though the perturbation treats every part's mass and cost as independent 0.5x-2x factors, so correlated errors (all rods share a linear density) are not modelled; the lines-metric tau values are presented in the results as findings although the README admits the lines ranking is tie-break noise. Disclaimer/AI-assistance statement present.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can rerun and extend it, and the next step (difficulty per line) is named. Nearest prior work: the sibling selfrep-closure (same BOM, closure under a shop) and selfrep-nextmachine (which machine to add next); this asks the single-part analogue. Result is close to a sort of qty x mass/cost: the NEMA17 motor dominating mass and cost closure follows directly from 5 motors at 280 g and 10 each in the BOM, and the finding that rankings by different metrics disagree is expected. Novelty is modest and not sourced against RepRap literature (no citation to closure/Moses/Chirikjian work or the RepRap BOM source in this README). Not publishable alone; useful as a sanity-check module of the programme.
evidence.domain: Compared with practice in self-replicating-machine / RepRap closure analysis: closure measured by mass and by cost is standard, additive per-line gains are a legitimate first-order model. Departures: no difficulty or process-capability model (a motor or controller is not learnable like a rod, as README admits), no accounting for the fact that learning a motor needs wire, magnets, laminations that become new imported feedstock (README says everything imported remains imported; learning a part would add feedstock lines), BOM units as 100-nut boxes not per-printer counts, no real measured masses. Rank stability uses independent log-uniform noise, not correlated or measured spreads; mean Kendall tau 0.87 is not given an interval. Mass of a 370 mm M8 rod at 110 g is plausible but unsourced.

defects.what: Tests do not pin any headline result and a mutation to the lines_to_reach threshold survives; a BOM or tie-break change would not fail any test
Lines-metric ranking is alphabetical tie-break; Kendall tau lines-vs-others in results.txt is therefore noise yet presented as a result
Stability analysis assumes independent per-part 0.5x-2x noise; correlated errors (shared rod linear density, shared vendor pricing) are not modelled, so 'fairly robust' is optimistic
No citation of prior self-replication closure literature or the RepRap BOM source; novelty of the question not positioned
Fragile relative sys.path import of sibling selfrep-closure while pyproject declares no dependencies; run.py has no main guard

verdict: A small, honest, reproducible calculation. Results reproduce exactly and four headline figures recompute independently from the BOM, and the README states its limits well, so correctness, completeness and claims reach 3. It misses the bar on verification (tests check identities, not results, and 1 of 4 seeded mutations survived) and on domain and fitness: the method is a sort of qty x mass or cost over assumed placeholder data with no difficulty model, no feedstock side effects and no literature positioning, so a RepRap-closure specialist would treat it as a sanity check, not a finding. Median 3 and correctness/claims at 3, but verification is 2, so it does not meet the bar; it is finished (completeness 3).
